Confession time!

I actually kind of suck at picking up things by ear. If I see what you're playing, I can copy it. If I can see what you're playing, I can even accompany it. I can improv over and between it, and things like that - 'cause I know how my guitar works and I know enough theory. I know why (to some extent) music works the way it does.

But...

If you ask me to pick up a new song, I really need the tab for it. I can read sheet, standard notation, but I can't sight-read it. I can (for the most part) sight-read tab, but I can't sight-read standard notation.

So, not only do I need tab (if you expect me to just play it in the studio and get it right in a short amount of time/with few takes), I can't play by ear.

It's a skill I envy.

When I tell people this, they are often surprised - and many musicians are also surprised to learn that I can't really play by ear.

They will often then ask me if I can fake it.

Well, that depends - like so many things.

Can I fake it for whom? Can I fake it for an audience? Probably - but unless I've practiced it with the band, I'm not going to try that with a paying audience. I think they deserve better than that. Can the band decide to play it in the "key of A minor" (or similar) and then me fake it? Not a chance - and absolutely not live.

Can I fake it for another musician who knows better? Nope...

I really don't like to even try to play by ear. I kinda suck at it. I've never been good at it. In December, I'll have been at it for 50 years. I'm unlikely to ever get good at it.

Do I wish I were good at it? Absolutely.

I could probably improve with a bunch of practice, but that's really unlikely to happen and it's not really a skill that's all that valuable for me to invest that much time in. Even then, I've done it and I'm pretty sure I'd never get really good at it - and I envy those people who can.

Like, I seriously envy it. I can't even tell something like thirds by ear - but I can by sight. If I see the guitarist's fingers, I can. By ear? Nope...
